text:
maria: odd one billing shows a large cost delta for project-olive. key used is from project-sage and the request passed through regional router that applies a cost-multiplier. I think attribution + per-route multipliers are being applied inconsistently. can we triage?

sam: can you paste headers/logs? is this the case where router annotates the request with a region tag and billing later multiplies token-cost by region?

maria: yes. repro: client->edge (key owner=project-sage)-> regional-router (adds X-Route-Region=eu-west; applies route-multiplier=1.2) -> auth exchange to sa in project-olive -> upstream sets X-Exec-Project=project-olive -> billing ingests exec project AND route multiplier. Logs:
```
12:01:02 auth: key=key_s owner=project-sage org=org-s
12:01:03 router: region=eu-west multiplier=1.2 preserve=X-Route-Region
12:01:04 proxy: exchanged->sa:sa-olive set X-Exec-Project=project-olive
12:01:05 billing: project=project-olive tokens=100 multiplier=1.2 cost=120
```
sam: ah. billing used exec project AND the multiplier. But client intended billing to go to key owner (project-sage) and owner shouldn't be charged by a region multiplier that was applied after the minting key.

kevin: operational risk: project-sage got overbilled relative to their quotas; project-olive saw logged usage but not billed. Also alert noise from quota exhaustion on project-sage.

jen: console UX nightmare: two projects show usage and numbers diverge. We should surface a provenance chain and a final "billing canonical" project in UI. Also explain how route multipliers are applied.

nina: policy question: should route multipliers be applied before or after we decide billing target? If billing target is key owner, maybe multiplier should be neutralized or moved to a per-request surcharge billed to route owner or router-service instead.

liam: we already have customers that intentionally bill execution project (parent org cases). So we need both modes. My proposal: canonicalization steps: 1) auth emits authoritative attribution envelope (owner=project-sage;exec=project-olive;route=eu-west;mult=1.2) 2) billing pipeline uses per-key flag `billing_canonical` (values: owner|exec|org-policy) to choose target; default=owner 3) multipliers are applied according to a policy: if billing target != owner, apply multiplier to chosen target; otherwise, multiplier becomes a router surcharge metric credited to router service budget (so owner isn't accidentally hit).

maria: sounds reasonable. Quick implement plan:
- short-term: auth should emit `X-Auth-Envelope: owner=project-sage;exec=project-olive;route=eu-west;mult=1.2` and a metric tag `auth.attrib.v2=owner:project-sage|exec:project-olive|route:eu-west|mult:1.2` sampled at 1% by default.
- mid-term: billing pipeline to consult `billing_canonical` on key metadata. If `owner`, then don't apply route multipliers to owner usage; instead add a separate `router_surcharge` line item attributed to router-service/infra. If `exec`, apply multiplier to exec target.
- console: display provenance chain and a toggle in key settings for `billing_canonical` with tooltip. Default to owner; warn about surcharges.

kevin: for sampling: baseline 0.5% global, but adaptive capture to 100% when we detect cost mismatch >5% between owner-accounted cost and exec-accounted cost in a 30m window for a key. That captures low-volume keys when they matter.

sam: agree. Also we need a reconciliation job to detect and correct any mischarged invoices during the migration window. Backfill logic: join billing rows with key registry to recompute canonical target and mark rows `attribution_recomputed=true` with a reason code.

jen: UX copy: in usage table show columns: minted-by, executed-as, route (with multiplier), billed-to. Hover explains how multipliers/surcharges work. I'll draft mockups.

nina: alerts: add rule to fire if router multipliers cause >10% variance in billed amount vs token-count normalized by owner for the same key over 1h. Also a low-sev alert for inconsistent X-Auth-Envelope across requests for same key (config drift).

liam: implementation owners:
- sam: add X-Auth-Envelope header + metric tag + tests (PR AUTH-6202)
- kevin: sampler + alert rules + reconciliation job plan (ticket BILL-331)
- maria: migration/backfill plan + invoice remediation runbook
- jen: console UX + key toggle copy + tooltip

ops-bot: @sam mentioned in eng-platform  created AUTH-6202 (emit X-Auth-Envelope + metric tag)

maria: one more edge-case: what if router multiplier is dynamic per-tenant (eg premium region)? we should store multiplier in attribution envelope as a decimal and keep provenance immutable once signed by auth so downstream can't reassign. Auth must sign or HMAC the envelope when passing to billing to prevent tampering.

sam: good point. we'll HMAC the envelope with internal key `AUTH_SIGNER_V2`. billing will verify signature before applying multiplier or will route multiplier to surcharge bucket if verification fails.

kevin: i'll add verification step in billing ingest and fail-safe to mark rows `pending_verification` if bad signature. Also include a monitoring dashboard for envelope verification failures.

maria: timeline: rapid header + sampling in 1 week, billing changes + reconciliation in 3 weeks, console + GA doc in 5 weeks. We'll do staging canary first.

jen: will post mockups in #design later today.

liam: opening PR today for header + HMAC and tests for verification.

maria: thanks team. this should keep billing predictable while preserving routing multipliers for cost accounting without surprising customers.
